messages:
maya: Heads up — our eval harness is producing nondeterministic outputs for the new 4-bit quantized model when top_p is enabled. 3/10 runs deviate from the golden. CI job: https://ci.internal/7254 :thinking_face:

sam: Ugh. Is seed being set at the request level or worker level? we had leaks when reusing worker processes before.

maya: We set seed here in runner.spawn_worker:
```python
# simplified
def spawn_worker(worker_id, base_seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(base_seed + worker_id)
    worker.rng = rng
```
But sampling still seems nonrepeatable when top_p triggered across batches.

anya: top_p is a bit tricky because we sample from a filtered distribution after softmax. If any in-place ops mutate the RNG or sampler state between requests, reuse will break determinism.

lee: Could also be multiple PRNGs in play — one for logits jitter (float noise) and one for categorical sampling. Are we using numpy in some parts and our C++ sampler elsewhere?

maya: Good call. The quantized kernel uses a fast C++ sampler for performance, but the eval harness calls numpy-based token filters pre-sampling. I suspect ordering changes between threads can lead to different RNG draws.

devon: I reproduced locally. If I force temperature=0 or disable top_p it becomes deterministic. So it's definitely sampling-related.

sam: Two quick fixes: 1) make a single per-request RNG and thread-safe copy it to every component before any sampling; 2) reseed per-sample deterministically (e.g., hash(request_id, step)). Both have perf tradeoffs.

maya: I'm leaning to #1 so we keep perf. Patch idea: create RequestRNG = RNG.from_seed(seed) and pass to quantized sampler API as RNG.handle (no global state).

ci-bot: build #7254 — job eval/flaky-tests failed (3 flakes) — https://ci.internal/7254/job/37 :exclamation:

anya: Also check top_p implementation: if we do cumulative-probability trim with floating rounding differences across quantized and fp kernels the cutoff index could be off by one, changing the candidate set and thus draws. That would explain 3/10.

lee: Great point. Compare the cutoff indices between fp and quantized runs using the same logits prefilter. Add an assert in debug mode: assert(set_fp_candidates == set_q_candidates)

maya: I'll add per-request RNG and the candidate-set assert to a debug build, run 50 seeds overnight. If it repros we can bisect kernel diff.

devon: If it still fails, try deterministic top_p fallback: pick highest-prob token on ties — helps identify if ties/rounding are the culprit.

maya: Cool. I'll open a PR with the RNG plumbing and debug assertions. tagging @sam @anya for review.

sam: Thanks — I'll review tomorrow. If we want a short-term workaround in CI, add a matrix job that sets sampling=greedy for quantized-eval to gate flakes while we fix.

maya: Added an issue: https://triage.internal/RED-4312 — "quantized eval nondeterminism with top_p".

ci-bot: Note: queued rerun for build #7254 (rerun by maya)

anya: Nice. If you want, I can instrument logs to output the top-10 cands and RNG state hash per step for failing runs. That'll speed root-cause. :mag_right:

maya: Please do, that would help a lot. Thanks everyone :pray:
